title: Automated changelog and customer-journey playbook for deprecations
creator: Leah Kim
description: Objective: build an orchestrated, partly-automated playbook that generates release notes, customer-facing changelogs, migration steps, and per-customer migration journeys for model and API deprecations. Scope includes automated changelog generation from PR metadata, templated migration guides, staged email and in-console comms, and a tracking dashboard for customer opt-ins and blocked upgrades. Out of scope: full auto-migration of customer workloads (technical work will be tracked in ENG-4399).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Discovery, 2025-11-06 to 2025-11-14): validate data sources (release PRs, CHANGELOG.md, deploy tags, telemetry), interview 6 customer accounts with pinned versions.
Phase 1 (Core automation MVP, 2025-11-17 to 2025-12-05): implement changelog generator service (backend), changelog templates, and initial release-notes pipeline integration; owners: PM/ENG/Docs.
Phase 2 (Customer journeys, 2025-12-06 to 2025-12-20): create per-customer migration templates, in-console banners, and email templates; run dry-run with 3 beta customers.
Phase 3 (GTM and docs, 2025-12-21 to 2026-01-10): coordinate support, solutions, and sales enablement; publish migration guides and release notes automation docs.
Phase 4 (Launch & monitoring, 2026-01-11 to 2026-01-15): cutover to using generated changelogs for deprecation announcement; monitor dashboard and open support tickets triage.
communication_timeline: T-minus 30 days: internal brief to Sales, Support, Solutions, Legal with embargoed release notes (via Confluence).
T-minus 21 days: publish public migration guide draft to docs.redwood.ai and request review from Applied ML and Runtime Eng.
T-minus 14 days: send targeted emails to customers with pinned deployments; include per-customer migration checklist link.
T-minus 7 days: in-console banner appears for affected customers with one-click link to migration playbook.
Launch day: public release notes, blog post, changelog entry auto-generated and published; social and partner comms go live.
Post-launch +7 days: follow-up email to customers that haven’t started migration with an invite to migration office hours.
release_notes_bullets: Automated changelog generation: release notes will be compiled from PR tags, release branches, and runtime compatibility metadata.
Per-customer migration checklist: personalized next-steps surfaced in the Console for pinned deployments.
Backwards-compatible gateway: runtime will route deprecated-vX callers to compatibility variant for a 90-day window (configurable).
Rollout telemetry: surface migration progress and failures in PM dashboard (tokenized customer IDs only).
migration_guides: GitHub repo with automated changelog tooling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/changelog-generator (RFC branch: feature/pm-10321)
acceptance_criteria: Changelog generator passes integration tests and produces templated HTML + markdown outputs for 95% of release PRs in test window.
Console banners render correctly for three tested customer accounts and link to the right migration guide versions.
Support, Sales, and Solutions receive and sign off on GTM playbook and email templates.
Tracking dashboard shows per-customer migration state and surfaces top 5 migration blockers within 48 hours of rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mismatched PR metadata leads to incorrect changelog entries. Mitigation: fall back to manual review queue and label BAD_CHANGELOG for human triage.
Risk: high number of pinned customers cause support spike. Mitigation: prioritize high-touch customers and schedule migration office hours + SRE runbook.
Risk: legal/compliance concerns about email cadence. Mitigation: loop Legal on templates and include unsubscribe/opt-out in all messages.
Risk: automation outputs PII in changelog. Mitigation: generator sanitizes fields and logs only tokenized IDs; security review required for telemetry endpoints.
